en.title: The Odyssey Dominates IMAX Screens Through September, Shattering Records
en.summary: Christopher Nolan's latest cinematic achievement, **The Odyssey**, is extending its exclusive IMAX run for an additional month. This decision comes as the film continues to break box office records and solidify its place as IMAX's biggest success story.
en.body:
## IMAX's Unstoppable Force

Christopher Nolan's **The Odyssey** is proving to be an unstoppable force on IMAX screens, with the film now confirmed to continue its exclusive run through the end of September. This extension marks a significant victory for the director and the premium large-format theater company, especially as competition for coveted IMAX screens intensifies each year. Studios increasingly rely on these larger, immersive presentations to draw audiences willing to pay a premium, a strategy **The Odyssey** has capitalized on with unprecedented success.

The film has already achieved the status of IMAX's highest-grossing release ever, a testament to both Nolan's directorial vision and the audience's appetite for his signature grand-scale filmmaking. Shot entirely on IMAX 70mm cameras, **The Odyssey** was tailor-made for the format, offering expansive visuals and a visceral sound experience that simply cannot be replicated on standard screens. This deep synergy between filmmaker and format is a key reason behind IMAX's decision to grant it an extended stay.

## A Blockbuster's Long Shadow

The extended run for **The Odyssey** means it will continue to occupy prime IMAX real estate, potentially squeezing out showings for other highly anticipated blockbusters. While specific titles haven't been confirmed for September, the AV Club noted that it could impact films like **Resident Evil** and **Avengers Endgame: Encore**. This situation is reminiscent of past IMAX battles, such as **Dune: Part Three** reportedly boxing out **Avengers: Doomsday** from December IMAX slots, even prompting Disney to develop its own "Infinity Vision" grading scheme. The sheer box office power of **The Odyssey** makes it difficult for IMAX to deny its continued presence.

Fans have responded with overwhelming enthusiasm for the film's extended theatrical life. The initial premiere tickets in select cities reportedly sold out rapidly, underscoring the demand for this specific viewing experience. For many, seeing **The Odyssey** on an IMAX 70mm screen is not just watching a movie, but participating in a cinematic event that honors Nolan's commitment to the theatrical medium. The film's ability to transcend its initial release window and maintain such a strong presence speaks volumes about its impact on audiences and the industry.

## What's Next

With **The Odyssey** guaranteed to dominate IMAX screens through September, audiences are encouraged to secure their tickets for this record-breaking cinematic experience. Further details regarding specific showtimes and potential competition for screens in the latter half of the month will likely emerge as September approaches.

content_raw: The battle for America’s limited supply of certified IMAX screens has become an increasingly fractious one in recent years, as studios have all quietly acknowledged that slapping their films onto bigger screens supported by louder sound systems is one of the only reliable ways to get audiences to shell out extra for a viewing. (It’s a more reliable money making strategy than trying to invent ever-more sexualized popcorn buckets, leastways.) Few directors are more in tune with the Canadian theater company’s whole deal, meanwhile, than Christopher Nolan, who not only favors the kinds of big, expansive shots that lend themselves to the biggest theatrical presentations possible, but also literally filmed his latest movie, The Odyssey , on the company’s 70mm cameras. Which probably goes some way toward explaining why IMAX has decided that, sure,  The Odyssey  can have its screens for a little longer, as  Variety  reports that Nolan’s movie has just extended its run in the format. The film will now stay on IMAX through the end of September, where it’ll likely squeeze out at least some showings for both  Resident Evil and  Avengers Endgame: Encore , which we have to assume made somebody at Disney’s eye twitch just the teensiest bit. (The company was already mad enough that Dune: Part Three  boxed  Avengers: Doomsday  out of IMAX theaters this December that most people assume it invented its own “Infinity Vision” theater grading scheme just to try to score some of that “premium showing” money off of moviegoers for itself.) It’s hard to blame IMAX, though:  The Odyssey  has been the format’s biggest box office success ever, making more on the company’s screens than the vast majority of other movies make in theaters, period. (To the tune of $457 million and counting, more than doubling  Avatar ‘s previous record-setting IMAX haul back in 2009.) That includes $66 million alone from IMAX’s massive 70mm screens, of which there are only 41 in the world; call it marketing, or filmmaking brio, or just the natural human desire to see the biggest possible version of Matt Damon’s face, but audiences embraced the idea that The Odyssey  on IMAX was an event, and the company is clearly happy to let the good times keep rolling for another month.
